decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: With inflation well above 2 percent and a strong labor market, the Committee expects it will soon be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed language about waiting for labor market conditions to reach maximum levels, signaling that rate hikes are likely coming soon because inflation is high and the job market is strong.

changes.quote: The Committee decided to continue to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases, bringing them to an end in early March.
changes.explanation: The Fed is officially putting a firm end date on its pandemic-era bond buying stimulus program.

changes.quote: Beginning in February, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $20 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $10 billion per month.
changes.explanation: The Fed halved the amount of new bonds it buys each month compared to the previous pace, stepping down its market support.

changes.quote: Indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen.
changes.explanation: The Fed streamlined its assessment by removing an older reference to prior policy support.

changes.quote: The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months but are being affected by the recent sharp rise in COVID-19 cases.
changes.explanation: Pandemic-sensitive sectors face renewed headwinds from the recent surge in virus cases.

tone_quotes.quote: With inflation well above 2 percent and a strong labor market, the Committee expects it will soon be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate.
The Committee decided to continue to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases, bringing them to an end in early March.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.54% APR costs about $60.58 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.85% and moved +7 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.45% would rise by about $11.71 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 682k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 7.2% over the past year (December 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +11 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.15%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.06% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed is preparing to start raising interest rates at upcoming meetings. As an educational note, the forecast model gave the next meeting odds as: hold 15%, cut 0%, hike 85%.

citations.detail: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.
